name: for-the-best-ex
description: Cut the patterns that make writing read as machine-written, then put a person back into it.

interface.shortDescription: Delete the tells. Put a person back in.
interface.longDescription:
Most tools that clean up AI writing only subtract. They strip the banned words, the throat-clearing, the fake-profound ending, and hand back prose that is clean and still reads as machine-written. Clean is not the same as human.

This skill does the subtraction, then does the part nobody does: it adds the things machine prose never has. A first-person stance. An anecdote with an institution and a date in it. An admission that you might be wrong. Sentence lengths that swing from four words to forty instead of sitting at a tidy eighteen. Hedges like "probably" and "I think" that polished output strips out.

Forked from no-ai-slop by Peter Yang, and extended with a rule layer drawn from published work on how machine-text detection actually operates.
